title: Machine Code Format
statement: A code format specifies a type of machine codes, a type of transition tables for each natural number $n$, a state-count function, an assembly operation taking $n$, an initial state in $\text{Fin}(n+1)$, and a table, and fixed serializations for codes and tables. It also provides table-reading and erased table-skipping operations, a natural-number guard, and a fallback code. These data satisfy the following conditions: assembled machines have state count $n$; their serialization is the pair encoding of the binary representation of $n$ followed by the unary encoding of the initial state and the table bits; every code is assembled from some such data; reading a table's bits followed by any suffix recovers that table and suffix; every successful table read splits its input into those table bits followed by the returned remainder; erasing the result of table reading agrees with skipping; and every table's bit length is at least the guard times $n+1$.
